solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Celeb initially involved with A-list – the runs a big feature of this

definitions.text: runs a big feature of this
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the sport rather than a plain synonym

indicators.note: what comes initially is at the very start, so only the opening letter is kept
things involved are tangled up together, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
taken as written, hyphen dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity mixes with the A-list crowd at a big sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash marks where the wordplay stops: everything after it describes the sport, in which track races are a central part.
explanation.definitionFit: Track and field competition is built around sprints and distance races, so running events are a major part of the sport.

clue.text: Scrap, with Labour leader moving a bit to the right – should get a medal!

indicators.text: Labour leader moving a bit to the right
indicators.note: shifting one letter a single step rightwards swaps it with its neighbour, turning that pair around

blocks.note: a sliver is a small scrap or splinter

explanation.surface: Someone praises a fight, or a Labour leader edging rightwards politically, as worthy of an award.
explanation.walkthrough: The Labour leader is the first letter L of SLIVER; moving it one place right past the I gives SILVER. The surface sneers at a party leader drifting to the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Second place in a competition earns the silver award, so the precious metal names that particular prize.

clue.text: Hackneyed load of balls due to be recycled with Sun's involvement

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade, so these letters are reformed in a fresh order
involvement brings an extra element into the mix, so one more letter joins the jumble

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: A tired story, nonsense due to be rehashed with help from the Sun tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Load of balls' reads as rubbish, but in cricket an over is six deliveries. The Sun suggests the newspaper; here it is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackneyed phrase is one worn out through repetition, so it has been employed far too often.

clue.text: When you're ready to erupt, stuff lion in big top

indicators.note: to stuff is to cram things in roughly, leaving the letters jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A circus act where an angry lion is crammed into the tent, about to explode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a positional word putting the lion inside the tent, but it is part of the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, reaching this stage means your temper is at the limit and you are about to lose control.

clue.text: Fish – royal tucked into seconds

indicators.note: something tucked into a place is put inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: Kate is the Princess of Wales
S is the abbreviation for second, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A royal tucking into a second helping of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' suggests eating; here it means placed inside. KATE goes between the two S's.
explanation.definitionFit: Skate is a flat ray-like fish eaten widely in Britain, and fish can be read as a plural noun.

clue.text: (& 24dn.) Toss chap off for immediate payment

indicators.note: something off is wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Paying someone off on the spot to get rid of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toss' looks like a verb acting on the chap, but both words simply supply letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Money handed over at the moment of sale, without credit or delay, is the commercial term for payment on delivery.

clue.text: Article about that is very appropriate

definitions.note: a verb here, to take for oneself

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the others

blocks.note: the definite article
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on a topic that is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective meaning suitable but is the verb meaning to take; i.e. is the standard abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take it without permission, which is stealing.

clue.text: Balls hoisted after Labour gets excited

blocks.note: labour is work
Ed Balls is a former Labour politician
something hoisted is raised up

explanation.surface: A Labour politician rising in the party makes members excited.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls was a Labour shadow chancellor; his first name stands for him. 'After' places ED UP behind WORK.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agitated or emotionally aroused is the idiomatic meaning of this phrasal adjective.

clue.text: Make out with promiscuous 'Cinders'

indicators.note: promiscuous means indiscriminate and mixed up, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Snogging a loose Cinderella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make out' suggests kissing, but it means to perceive. Cinders is Cinderella's nickname, used here only for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To make out a distant shape is to perceive or recognise it with some effort.

clue.text: Lord, the PM's active on Right Bank!

blocks.note: live means active or switched on
R is the abbreviation for right
a pool is a shared fund or bank of money

explanation.surface: A peer who is prime minister is busy on the Paris Right Bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right Bank' suggests Paris; the two words separate into R and POOL. Lord Liverpool was British prime minister from 1812 to 1827.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Liverpool held the premiership for fifteen years, so the title names that former head of government.

clue.text: See 18ac.
Unconventional dresser with fixed box

blocks.note: TV is short for transvestite
set means fixed or settled

explanation.surface: Someone with odd taste in clothes owns a built-in cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dresser' suggests a piece of furniture beside a box, but it is a person who dresses oddly. 'The box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Box is informal slang for a television receiver, from the shape of early sets.

clue.text: Amazingly, Trump's giving away millions, getting thinner!

indicators.note: to give something away is to part with it, so a letter is dropped
something amazing defies expectation, so the letters end up in a surprising order

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A miracle: Trump is donating his fortune and losing weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M from TRUMPS and rearrange. 'Thinner' looks like slimming but is the paint solvent; turps is short for turpentine.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpentine is used to dilute oil paint and clean brushes, which makes it a paint solvent.

clue.text: Net is controlled, in the clutches of titled person – shady

indicators.note: something controlled is manipulated, so the letters are worked into another order
to be in someone's clutches is to be held by them, so one piece lies inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: The internet is in the grip of some aristocrat, which seems dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: The holder does not have to split evenly: here the rearranged letters go in after the title's second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady and sinister both describe something suspicious or menacing, suggesting dishonest intent.

clue.text: In the Eye, Blair's back in as a dry alternative competitor

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters are turned round
an alternative version is a different arrangement of the same letters
one piece placed in another sits within it

blocks.note: Private Eye ran Blair as the Rev Tony, vicar of St Albion's
taken as written

explanation.surface: Private Eye says Tony Blair is back as a rival standing for temperance.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical magazine whose long-running parody cast Blair as a trendy vicar, so his title is REV. Reversed, it goes inside a rearrangement of AS A DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: An adversary is an opponent or rival, the person you compete against.

clue.text: Castle, possibly getting laid etc, erupted

indicators.note: an eruption throws material everywhere, leaving the letters scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Castle, a person's name perhaps, getting lucky and so on, then blowing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks the castle as one example of the answer rather than an exact synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress guarding a city, so a castle is one kind of stronghold that fits.

clue.text: Liberal peer, corseted in a bit, got thinner

indicators.note: a liberal reading takes freedoms, so the letters are freely rearranged
a corset encloses the body, so one piece is wrapped by another

blocks.note: taken as written
a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: A Lib Dem lord squeezed into a corset slims down a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal peer' looks like a Lib Dem lord, but Liberal is the rearrangement signal and the peer supplies only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to narrow gradually towards one end, so tapered means became narrower.

clue.text: (& 11dn.) NB. colossal need determined to crack Trump's replacement Apple policy?

indicators.note: something cracked is broken into pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written
Mike Pence, Trump's vice-president, would have replaced him

explanation.surface: A huge craving to break Trump's successor, then a jab at Apple's business practice.
explanation.walkthrough: Pence was vice-president under Trump. The question mark flags that the definition is a pointed example: Apple is often accused of designing phones to go out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Designing products with a deliberately limited lifespan so customers must buy again is the practice Apple is often accused of.

clue.text: One time politician strangles north eastern lawyer

indicators.note: strangling grips round the throat, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a means one
T is the abbreviation for time
a Tory is a Conservative
NE is the abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A former politician attacks a lawyer from the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One time' looks like 'one-time', meaning former, but splits into A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: An attorney is a legal representative, the American term for a practising solicitor or advocate.

clue.text: Chaotic end of Trump era ends with kiss-off – time to relax

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept
chaos is total disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: last letter of the word
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The messy close of Trump's presidency ends with a dismissal, and now everyone can unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kiss-off' means a dismissal, but only KISS is used for letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the drinking and socialising at a resort after a day on the slopes, a period of leisure.

clue.text: The thinking bather's ejaculation

blocks.note: surface reading: something smutty about a man in the bath
setter's reading: an ejaculation is an exclamation, the cry of Archimedes in his bath on solving a problem

explanation.walkthrough: Archimedes supposedly leapt from his bath crying out on discovering the principle of displacement. 'Ejaculation' in its old sense means a sudden exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek cry meaning 'I have found it' is the classic shout of a thinker making a discovery.

clue.text: Bill having Lewinsky mainly on end of the desk

indicators.note: mainly here points to the head of the word, so its leading letter is taken
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a tab is a bill, as in a bar tab
leading letter of the name
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton and Monica Lewinsky on the Oval Office desk.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like Clinton, but it is a tab, as in a restaurant bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk is a piece of furniture with a flat working surface, essentially a writing table.

clue.text: Nebuchadnezzar's guts?

blocks.note: first meaning: a very large wine container holding twenty standard measures
second meaning: courage, in British slang, as in losing your nerve

explanation.walkthrough: The king of Babylon is a red herring: a nebuchadnezzar is a giant champagne size. In British slang, having the guts to do something is having bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a glass container for wine and, informally in Britain, nerve or courage.

clue.text: One who tends to precede Brenda with "banger"

blocks.note: a banger is an old, battered car
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Someone who usually walks ahead of a woman called Brenda, carrying a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tends' looks like 'is inclined', but it means looks after. Private Eye, a satirical British magazine, calls the late Queen Brenda, giving ER; a banger is British slang for a clapped-out car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after the sick, elderly or disabled, so tending to others is the job.

clue.text: See 6dn,
Inflammatory condition means record sex lives

blocks.note: to enter data is to record it
it is slang for sex or sex appeal
to live is to be, so lives gives is

explanation.surface: A medical condition flares up in people who keep a record of their sex lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives' looks like a plural noun after 'sex', but it is a verb meaning exists.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteritis is an inflammation of the intestine, so it is a medical swelling disorder of the gut.

clue.text: Mate with Punch, showing arrogance at first

indicators.note: what comes at first is placed in front, fixing which piece leads

blocks.note: side is an old word for swagger or pretentiousness
a drink's punch is its kick

explanation.surface: A friend throws a punch, behaving arrogantly from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: To put on side is a British idiom for acting superior, so side means swagger; the punch is the kick of a drink or a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a close companion or assistant, a friend who goes everywhere with you.

clue.text: Half of this groper's payment for service

blocks.clueFragment: Half of this groper's payment for service
blocks.note: surface reading: a lecher handing over money for a sexual service
setter's reading: the first three letters of the answer form a charge for professional work, and the whole word means a groper

explanation.walkthrough: The groper is the definition; the rest notes that the front half of the answer, FEE, is a payment for service.
explanation.definitionFit: A groper is someone who touches with the hands, literally one who feels.
